Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Young (19 y) female with acute dysuria, suprapubic discomfort, malodorous urine, and single episode of macroscopic hematuria. No fever, flank pain, nausea/vomiting, or urinary frequency/urgency.  
- Working diagnosis: Uncomplicated acute bacterial cystitis.  
- Differential diagnoses consistent with transcript and DDx:  
  • Uncomplicated acute cystitis (High likelihood) – classic presentation without systemic signs.  
  • Chlamydial/gonococcal urethritis or cervicitis (Moderate likelihood) – new sexual partner, no prior STI screen; minimal genital symptoms.  
  • Urolithiasis (Low likelihood) – one episode hematuria but lacks colicky/flank pain.  
- Management priorities: Empiric oral antibiotics, hydration advice, safety-net instructions for escalation, consideration of STI screening and pregnancy testing.  

Management Plan

- Prescribed course of antibiotics: Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days (exact drug to be finalized; route not documented).  
- Hydration advice: Increase fluid intake; consider cranberry juice.  
- Sexual activity: Advise abstaining until symptoms resolve; continue condom use thereafter.  
- Red-flag education: Return or call if fever, back/flank pain, worsening symptoms, or no improvement after completing antibiotics.  
- Pregnancy test: Advised if concern or symptoms persist.  
- Follow-up: If not improved by end of week (≈4–5 days), contact clinic for reassessment.  
- STI screen: Recommended but not documented as ordered; to be arranged at follow-up if indicated.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Uncomplicated acute cystitis – High likelihood: Acute onset dysuria, suprapubic pain, malodorous urine, hematuria; absence of systemic signs.  
2. Chlamydial/gonococcal urethritis or cervicitis – Moderate likelihood: New partner, no prior screening; dysuria can be urethritis; lacks discharge.  
3. Urolithiasis – Low likelihood: Hematuria supports; absence of flank/colicky pain makes less probable.
